title: Effects of low-level prenatal lead exposure on child IQ at 4 and 8 years in a UK birth cohort study.
ehr_evidence: The study sample was derived from the ALSPAC, a population-based study investigating environmental and genetic influences on the health, behaviour and development of children.
summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating the association between low-level prenatal lead exposure and child IQ at ages 4 and 8 years, including sex-specific effects and moderation by prenatal exposure.
key_findings: No association of prenatal lead exposure with child IQ at 4 or 8 years in adjusted regression models.
Positive association for IQ at age 8 years in girls: predicted increase per 1 mg/dl prenatal B-Pb was verbal 0.71 (p=0.021), performance 0.57 (p=0.099), and total 0.73 (p=0.017).
In boys, coefficients tended to be negative: verbal -0.15, performance -0.42, and total -0.29 points per 1 mg/dl (all p > 0.200).
No evidence for prenatal B-Pb moderating the association between child B-Pb and IQ at age 4 or 8 years.
population: Pregnant women and their offspring enrolled in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), UK
limitations: Small sample size for IQ at age 4 and moderation analysis
Potential measurement error in IQ tests due to child factors
Unmeasured confounders such as maternal and paternal IQ
Lack of data on concomitant exposure to other pollutants like cadmium
Unknown childhood lead exposure not accounted for
Single time-point prenatal blood sampling may not capture full gestational exposure
data_availability_statement: Data relating to prenatal lead exposure and child IQ at 4 and 8 years old in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children doi:http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.neuro.201 7.07.025 Data in Brief.
